manifestations.description: she "has still been suffering from severe low back pain with left leg sciatica, together with associated symptoms such as weakness, numbness and stiffness in the affected areas".

weakness, numbness and stiffness in the affected areas
She has to rely on painkillers and medical ointment to manage the persistent pain.
She is no longer able to return to her pre-accident job as a cleaner which requires strenuous manual work.
She was diagnosed with adjustment disorder with prolonged depressive reaction and the disorder was found to be causally related to the persistent low back pain.

source: She attended the Accident & Emergency Department of Kwong Wah Hospital on the same day. Her back pain persisted and she attended the A&E Department on nine more occasions in 2010.
She was referred for physiotherapy and occupational therapy.

treatments_received.treatment: referral to Department of Orthopaedics and Traumatology
source: She was also referred to the Department of Orthopaedics and Traumatology for management of her persistent back and left lower limb pain.
she has also developed mental symptoms and has been attending the West Kowloon Psychiatric Centre since January 2014.
As a result of this accident, the plaintiff was granted intermittent sick leave for the period between 23 January 2010 and 13 February 2010.
She was given intermittent sick leave of about 18 days between 13 October 2009 and 2 November 2009.
The plaintiff was granted intermittent sick leave during the period between 22 February 2010 and 10 December 2015.
